Ibn Juzayy, al-Tashil (commentary on Surah 54, verses 1–3):

﴿The Hour has drawn near, and the moon has been split.﴾ That is, the Resurrection has drawn near. Its drawing near means that a small amount of time remains for it compared to what has passed. For this reason the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) said: "I and the Hour have been sent like these two," and he pointed with his index and middle fingers.

﴿And the moon was split.﴾ This is a report of what occurred during the time of the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ). The Quraysh asked him for a sign, so he showed them the splitting of the moon. He (ﷺ) said: "Bear witness." Ibn Mas'ud said: "The moon was split, and I saw it in two parts, one part behind the mountain and the other part on this side of it." It has also been said that the meaning of "the moon was split" is that it will split on the Day of Resurrection. This is a false view, refuted by the sound hadiths that report the splitting of the moon. The Muslim community has agreed that it occurred, and the verse is interpreted accordingly, except by those whose opinion is not regarded.

﴿But if they see a sign, they turn away and say: "Continuous magic."﴾ The pronouns refer to the Quraysh, and the sign referred to is the splitting of the moon. At that point the Quraysh said: "Muhammad has bewitched the moon." The word mustamirr (continuous) means lasting, enduring. It has also been said that it means passing, going away soon. It has also been said that it means strong; on this meaning it derives from al-mirra, which is strength.

﴿And every matter will be settled.﴾ That is, everything must have an end: the truth will be established and falsehood will be defeated.

Ibn Juzayy (al-Tashil) on surah 54, verse 4:

﴿And there had certainly come to them of the news that which contains a deterrent﴾. "Al-anba'" (news, reports) here is intended to mean what has come in the Qur'an of narratives, proofs and admonitions. "Muzdajar" is a verbal noun (ism masdar) meaning "restraint" or "deterrence" (al-izdijar), or it is a noun of place, meaning that it is the place where one is expected to be restrained by it.

﴿Far-reaching wisdom﴾ is either a substitute (badal, a grammatical apposition) for what is in it, or the predicate of an omitted subject, meaning "it is far-reaching wisdom." ﴿Then of what use are the warnings?﴾ The word *mā* may be a negation, or it may be an interrogative for the sense of remoteness and denial.

So turn away from them. (﴿فَتَوَلَّ عَنْهُمْ﴾) That is, turn away from them, since you know that warning will not benefit them.

﴿On the day when the caller calls to a terrible thing,﴾ The factor (al-'amil) governing "day" (yawm) is an implied verb whose estimated form is: "Remember," or the phrase "﴿يَخْرُجُونَ﴾ (they will come forth)" that follows after it. The governing factor is not "﴿تَوَلَّ عَنْهُمْ﴾ (turn away from them)," for it would then be a point of pause. It has also been said that the meaning is: "﴿تَوَلَّ عَنْهُمْ﴾ (turn away from them)" on the day when the caller calls. The first view is more apparent and more well known.

The caller is Gabriel or Israfil, when he blows into the Trumpet. The "terrible thing" (al-shay' al-nukr) is the severe and dreadful matter. The word is derived from denial (al-inkar), meaning it is "unknown" (munkar), because no one has ever seen the like of it. What is meant is the Day of Resurrection.

﴿with their eyes downcast﴾ is a metaphor for humiliation. "Khushsha'an" is in the accusative as a circumstantial state (hal) of the pronoun in "﴿يَخْرُجُونَ﴾ (they come forth)."

﴿They will come forth from the graves,﴾ that is, from the tombs.

﴿as if they were scattered locusts.﴾ He compared them to locusts in their emergence from the earth, so it is as if this is an argument for resurrection, like the argument from the emergence of plants. It has also been said that he compared them to locusts only in their multitude, and that some of them surge over others.

[Qur'anic quotation]: ﴿Hastening forward⁠—⁠﴾... 

Let me be precise and follow the instructions: translate the passage faithfully.

﴿Hastening forward﴾, i.e., rushing (مسرعين). It is also said: gazing fixedly at the caller (ناظرين إلى الداع).

Commentary of Ibn Juzayy (al-Tashil) on surah 54, verse 9:

﴿So they denied Our servant﴾, meaning Nuh (peace be upon him), and he is described here as a servant to honour him and single him out. ﴿And they said, "He is mad, and he was rebuffed"﴾, that is, they rebuffed him with insults and threats, and said to him: ﴿"If you do not desist, O Nuh, you will surely be among those stoned to death."﴾ [al-Shu'ara': 116].

Commentary of Ibn Juzayy (al-Tashil) on surah 54, verse 10–14:

﴿So he called upon his Lord: "I am overpowered, so help [me]."﴾ Meaning: the disbelievers have overpowered me, so give me victory, or give victory to Yourself (i.e., to Your cause).

﴿So We opened the gates of the heaven with water pouring down.﴾ This is an expression for the abundance of rain, as though it were pouring out from gates. It was also said: gates were in fact opened in the sky on that day. Al-Munhamir means abundant.

﴿And the waters met﴾ the water of the sky and the water of the earth,

﴿for a matter that had been decreed.﴾ That is, it had been decreed in eternity (al-azal). It may also mean that it was measured by a known measure. It is narrated concerning this that the water rose above the earth by forty cubits (dhira').

﴿And We carried him on [a vessel] made of planks and nails.﴾ This means the ship, and al-dusur (nails) is the plural of dussar, the singular being dissar. It was also said that they are the front parts of the ship, and it was also said that they are its ribs; the first is the most well known.

﴿Sailing under Our eyes﴾ an expression for God's protection and care of it.

﴿As a reward for one who had been disbelieved.﴾ That is, a reward for Noah. It was also said: a reward for God the Exalted, and the first is more apparent. "Jaza'" (reward) is in the accusative as an object of purpose (maf'ul min ajlihi), and its governing element is what preceded it, namely the opening of the gates of the sky and the actions mentioned after it; that is, We made all of that a reward for Noah. It is possible that His saying "kafara" (disbelieved) means disbelief in the religion, and the sense would be: "for one who was disbelieved in" (li-man kafira bihi), with the pronoun omitted; or it may mean the disbelief in a blessing, because Noah, peace be upon him, was a blessing from God which his people denied, so in this case no omitted pronoun is needed.

Ibn Juzayy's commentary (al-Tashil) on surah 54, verse 15:

﴿And We have certainly left it as a sign﴾. The pronoun refers to the story mentioned, or to the deed, or to the ship. It is related in this sense that it remained on al-Judi until the earliest of this community looked upon it. ﴿So is there anyone who will be mindful?﴾ This is an exhortation (taḥḍīḍ) to remembrance, and in it is a beautiful gentleness (mulāṭafa) from God toward His servants. The word mudakkir is of the pattern mufta'il (مفتعل). Its original form was mudtakir (مدتكر), then the ta' was changed to dal (دال) and the dal was assimilated into it (idghām).
﴿So how was My punishment and My warnings?﴾ This is a rebuke in the form of a question (tawqif), containing a threat to the Quraysh. "Nudhur" is the plural of "nadhir" (warner).

Commentary of Ibn Juzayy (al-Tashil) on surah 54, verse 17–18:

﴿And We have certainly made the Qur'an easy for remembrance﴾. That is, We made it easy to memorize. This is known through observation, for young children and others memorize it thoroughly, unlike other books. It has been narrated that no scripture of God was memorized by heart except the Qur'an. It was also said: the meaning of the verse is that We made it easy to understand and to be admonished by it, because of the proofs and the eloquent wisdom it contains. He repeated this eloquent verse, and His saying ﴿So taste My punishment and warnings﴾ [al-Qamar: 37, 39], to alert the listener at each story, so that he may take a lesson from it, since each story that was mentioned is a lesson and an admonition. He concluded each one with what awakens the listener through the threat in His saying ﴿Then how was My punishment and warning?﴾, and with gentle kindness in His saying ﴿And We have certainly made the Qur'an easy for remembrance, so is there any who will remember?﴾.

Commentary of Ibn Juzayy (al-Tashil) on surah 54, verse 19:

﴿A furious wind (rīḥan ṣarṣaran)﴾: meaning, one with a loud, roaring sound, so it is derived from ṣarīr, meaning sound. It was also said: its meaning is cold, so it is derived from ṣirr (cold). ﴿On a day of continuous ill omen﴾. It is narrated that it was a Wednesday, until some of them considered that every Wednesday is an ill-omened day. And they narrated: the last Wednesday of the month is a day of continuous ill omen.

Commentary of Ibn Juzayy (al-Tashil) on surah 54, verse 20:

﴿Tanzi'u al-nas﴾ (It uproots the people): meaning, it tears them up from their places. ﴿As if they were trunks of uprooted palm trees﴾ (ka'annahum a'jaza nakhlin munqa'ir). They perished by this, because they were tall, large-bodied, like palm trees. It was also said: the wind used to cut off their heads, so that bodies remained without heads, and He likened them to the trunks of palm trees, since these are without branches. It was also said: they had dug pits to protect themselves from the wind, and they perished in them, so He likened them to palm trunks when they are lying in their pits.

Commentary of Ibn Juzayy (al-Tashil) on surah 54, verse 24:

﴿أَبَشَراً﴾ is Salih (peace be upon him), and it is in the accusative by a suppressed verb. The meaning is that they denied that they should follow a human being, and they demanded that the messenger be from among the angels. Then they added to this by denying that they should follow one man, while they were a large group. ﴿وَسُعُرٍ﴾ means obstinacy (ʿinad). It was also said that it means madness (junun), and it was said that it means anxiety and grief (hamm wa ghamm). Its root is from al-saʿir (the blaze), meaning fire, as if the soul were burning up with worry.

Ibn Juzayy, *al-Tashil*, on Surah 54, verse 25:

﴿Has the reminder been sent down upon him from among us?﴾ They denied that God would single him out for prophethood instead of them, and that was ignorance on their part, for bounty is in God's hand; He gives it to whom He wills. ﴿Insolent﴾: wanton and arrogant.

Commentary of Ibn Juzayy (al-Tashil) on surah 54, verse 28:

﴿And inform them that the water is to be shared between them﴾. That is, for them is one day, and for the she-camel is one day, without them transgressing against the she-camel. So the pronoun in ﴿inform them﴾ refers to Thamud, and to the she-camel by way of giving precedence to rational beings (taghlib). It was also said: the pronoun refers to Thamud, and the meaning is that some of them should not transgress against others. ﴿Every drinking shall be attended﴾, that is, witnessed.

Commentary of Ibn Juzayy (al-Tashil) on surah 54, verse 29:

﴿So they called to their companion﴾ meaning: the one who hamstrung the she-camel, whose name was Qudar, and he was the most red-faced (ahmar) of Thamud and the most wretched of them. ﴿And he took (it) in hand﴾ meaning he dared to commit a great matter, namely hamstringing the she-camel. It was said: "taʿaṭṭā" means he took up the sword.

Commentary of Ibn Juzayy (al-Tashil) on surah 54, verse 31:

﴿صَيْحَةً وَاحِدَةً﴾ ("a single cry"): Jibril cried out with a cry, and they died from it. ﴿فَكَانُواْ كَهَشِيمِ ٱلْمُحْتَظِرِ﴾ ("so they became like the crushed debris of the one who builds an enclosure"). Al-hashim (the crushed debris) is what is broken and crumbled of trees and other things. Al-muhtazir (the one who builds an enclosure) is the one who makes a hazirah (an enclosure), which is a wall of branches or reeds or the like, or it may be a pen for livestock or a dwelling. So Allah likened Thamud, when they perished, to what crumbles from the enclosure of leaves and other things. It was also said: al-muhtazir is al-muhtariq (the one who burns).

Ibn Juzayy's commentary (al-Tashil) on surah 54, verses 36–37:

﴿So they disputed about the warnings﴾ – tashakkaku (they doubted/were skeptical).

His people had thought that they were human beings, and they wanted from them the abomination (al-fahisha). So Allah obliterated their eyes, and they became level with their faces. It was also said: the obliteration (al-tams) means that they could not see them, and that they entered Lut's house and did not see anyone in it.

It was also said: the obliteration (al-tams) means that they could not see them, and that they entered Lut's house and did not see anyone in it.

Commentary of Ibn Juzayy (al-Tashil) on surah 54, verse 43:

﴿Are your disbelievers better than those [former ones]?﴾ This is an address to the Quraysh in the manner of a threat. The hamza (interrogative particle) here is for denial, and its meaning is: Are the disbelievers among you better in the sight of God than the earlier disbelievers mentioned, such that We destroyed them when they denied the messengers, while you will be saved though you have denied your messengers? Rather, the One who destroyed them will destroy you. ﴿Or do you have an immunity in the Scriptures?﴾ Its meaning: Or do you have an immunity from punishment in the Book of God?
﴿Or do they say, "We are a united company, victorious"?﴾ That is: "We will gather together and defend ourselves by fighting."

Ibn Juzayy's commentary (al-Tashil) on Surah 54, verse 45:

﴿Soon will the multitude be put to flight, and they will turn their backs.﴾ This is a promise from God to His Messenger that He will defeat the host of Quraysh, and that has become evident on the Day of Badr and in the conquest of Makkah.

Commentary of Ibn Juzayy (al-Tashil) on surah 54, verse 47–49:

﴿Indeed, the criminals are in error and madness.﴾ By "the criminals" here are meant the disbelievers, and their error is in this world, while the "suʿr" (blaze, burning) is for them in the Hereafter, and it is burning. It was also said: he meant by "the criminals" the Qadariyyah (the Qadariyya, those who deny divine predestination), because of His words in refuting them: ﴿Indeed, all things We have created with qadar (measure, decree).﴾ The first view is more apparent.

﴿They will be dragged through the Fire﴾, meaning they will be pulled along in it.

﴿Indeed, all things We have created with qadar.﴾ The meaning is that Allah created every thing with qadar, that is, with a known decree preceding in eternity (al-azal). It is possible that the meaning of ﴿bi-qadar﴾ is "in due measure" regarding its form, its attributes and other than that, but the first is more preferred, and in it is a proof for the People of the Sunnah (Ahl al-Sunnah) against the Qadariyyah. The phrase "kulla shay'" (every thing) is in the accusative because of a verb implied, which is explained by "khalaqnahu" (We created it).

Commentary of Ibn Juzayy (al-Tashil) on surah 54, verse 50–55:

﴿And Our command is but one, like a glance of the eye.﴾ This is an expression for the swiftness of creation and the effectiveness of Allah's command. The "one" (wāḥida) is meant as the word, which is His saying "Be" (kun).

﴿And We had certainly destroyed your like (ashyā'akum)﴾, meaning your counterparts (ashyā'akum) from among the disbelievers.

﴿And everything they did is in the scriptures (zubur)﴾, i.e., everything they did is recorded in the books of deeds.

﴿Recorded (mustaṭar)﴾, i.e., written, and it is from al-saṭr (line, writing). You say "saṭṭartu" and "istaṭartu" with the same meaning. What is meant is the small and the great of their deeds. It was also said: all things.

﴿And rivers﴾, meaning rivers of water, wine, milk, and honey, and he suffices with the generic noun.

﴿In a seat of truth (maqʿad ṣidq)﴾, i.e., in a place that is pleasing.
